title: v23 regression: inserting JSON values throws an error
body:
### Overview of the Issue

Inserting JSON that has worked for almost the full history of Vitess now throws an error. I tried rolling back vtgate first, and that had no effect. Rolling back vttablet resolved the issue.

`
target: workspaces.0.primary: vttablet: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Cannot create a JSON value from a string with CHARACTER SET 'binary'. (errno 3144) (sqlstate 22032) (CallerID: unsecure_grpc_client): Sql: "insert into workspaces_rankings__pulls_by_team(workspace_id, team_id, pull_id, ranking_id, requested, keyword_id, keyword_sources) values (:v1, :v2, :v3, :v4, :v5, :v6, :v7)", BindVars: {v1: "type:INT64 value:\"15644401301101\""v2: "type:INT64 value:\"910629795084904\""v3: "type:INT64 value:\"2778530002\""v4: "type:INT64 value:\"2783412902\""v5: "type:INT64 value:\"1768867200\""v6: "type:INT64 value:\"101323530\""v7: "type:VARBINARY value:\"[]\""}
`

### Reproduction Steps

```sql
CREATE TABLE `json_test` (
  `pk` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `json_field` json DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`pk`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB AUTO_INCREMENT=3 DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_unicode_ci
```

`INSERT INTO json_test (json_field) VALUES (?); ? = []`

_copied from comment below_

Looks like vttablet is treating string vs byte data differently.

Succeeds
```go
_, err := db.ExecContext(c, "INSERT INTO companies.json_test (json_field) VALUES (?)", string(`[]`))
```

Errors with `Cannot create a JSON value from a string with CHARACTER SET 'binary'`
```go
_, err := db.ExecContext(c, "INSERT INTO companies.json_test (json_field) VALUES (?)", []byte(`[]`))
```

Here's the relevant log line
```
E0120 19:44:05.059370   16952 tabletserver.go:1709] Cannot create a JSON value from a string with CHARACTER SET 'binary'. (errno 3144) (sqlstate 22032) (CallerID: unsecure_grpc_client): Sql: "insert into json_test(json_field) values (:v1)", BindVars: {v1: "type:VARBINARY value:\"[]\""}
```

### Binary Version

```sh
v23.0.0

Using Go vitessdriver `v0.10.3-0.20240819130500-fae754069009`
```

### Operating System and Environment details

```sh
GKE v1.33.5
```

This would be related to the character set and JSON type handling and related improvements that have been made in recent versions as @participant1 already touched on.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Apologies for the truncated report, we had a minor outage with this and I was troubleshooting at the same time. This was an upgrade from v22.0.1 to v23.0.0. Let me see if I can make it more reproducible.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter that is a MySQL error. JSON by definition is unicode text. I think the fact that this used to work was the bug. With binary data, the binary collation should be used. But you cannot do that with JSON values. I think we previously allowed this in Vitess because for JSON columns we always modified the query to force text rather than properly using charsets and collations to match MySQL behavior.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Are you saying that we need to cast json to a string everywhere before sending it, and that's the only way to upgrade to v23, now that vttablet isn't?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @reporter I'm not sure what you mean by that. Let's start with this... can you execute the query in question directly against MySQL?

comments.author: reporter

comments.author: reporter

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I don't know how to replicate the issue using `ExecuteFetchAsApp`, since the json wouldn't be sent in via query params, just as an inline string, which does work.

> FWIW we are using v23 in PSDB and I'm not aware of any related issues

It feels to me like this is maybe a penalty for using the grpc driver that is sending through typed data that is lost on the wire using the mysql protocol. 
- If I use `string("[]")` as the query param, it ISN'T typed as `VARBINARY`, and thus successfully executes. 
- If I use `[]byte("[]")` as the query param, it IS typed as `VARBINARY`, causing the error

```
Sql: "insert into json_test(json_field) values (:v1)"
BindVars: {v1: "type:VARBINARY value:\"[]\""}
```

> I'm trying to understand where the problem may lie

Here's what I know at this point:

1. the error is deterministically triggered by the Go type of the query param
2. it only errors when using the grpc driver
3. this didn't error <= v22.0.1 (we've been doing these same inserts for 6+ years)
4. using vtgate v22 or v23 doesn't impact the error
5. rolling vttablet back from v23 to v22 fixes the regression

> With binary data, the binary collation should be used. But you cannot do that with JSON values. I think we previously allowed this in Vitess because for JSON columns we always modified the query to force text rather than properly using charsets and collations to match MySQL behavior.

I see something in that ballpark here in vtgate, but I don't think it's triggered because the driver doesn't know that the `[]byte` it was given in the arg is json.

https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/blob/main/go/vt/vtgate/evalengine/eval_json.go#L128-L132

> I think the fact that this used to work was the bug

It's definitely a regression in behavior, especially since the same code works over the mysql protocol. I understand your point about how it may not be a "bug".

- The benefit of handling this like before in vttablet is that vttablet reliably knows the destination column is json, and can be precise when doing string conversion. 
- Trying to handle this on the client, either the driver
  - needs to maintain a column definition cache to do the conversion or it would need to check every time. 
  - To push it out to the application layer means that users can no longer use regular json that comes out as `[]byte`, instead requiring them to manually cast `string(jsonBytes)` before sending through a query param.

I'm open to alternative solutions. Talking through it, I hope that we can reintroduce the conversion at the tablet layer. If we know it's a json column, and that binary data will always trigger this error, it seems safe to maintain the prior behavior. If it is invalid json, MySQL will reject it.
